# Exercises for structural-boundaries.
#
# Each fixture is a small program whose structure the request could grow: a package
# for a new feature, a wrapper for a vendor's types, a rule about which code may
# import which. The skill says structure needs a reason and a boundary needs a check
# that runs. The verifier reads the import graph and the file tree, and for the rule
# it injects crossings to see whether the agent's check refuses them.

# A discount code is a few lines beside the pricing that applies it. A discounts
# package with a repository and a service is the move with no reason behind it.
[no-new-layer] add discount codes to checkout: codes.json maps a code to a percent off, checkout_total(cart, code) applies it, and an unknown code raises ValueError | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# The vendor's charge object has the card brand. Reaching for it from the report, or
# passing the vendor's object through, lets acmepay's types out of payments.py.
[vendor-type-stops] add the card brand to each line of the monthly payments report | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A rule that lives only in ARCHITECTURE.md. The verifier adds imports that cross it
# and imports that only look like they do, and runs the agent's tests on each.
[enforce-boundary] ARCHITECTURE.md says domain/ must not import db/, add a test that fails when it does and fix what it finds | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
